body:
## Problem

`adlc ticket doctor` reports `store:storehash-manifest-bind — MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID` on this repository whenever `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` is exported. The manifest is not corrupt.

Measured on main: `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` holds 271 entries. Lines 1-95 (2026-07-23 to 2026-07-26) carry no `sig` field at all; line 96 (2026-07-27) is the first signed entry, and everything after it is signed. All 28 segments under `.adlc/manifest.d/` are fully signed. `adlc gate-manifest verify --allow-legacy-unsigned` reports `manifest ok (388 entries, 28 segments)`, and `adlc ticket doctor` with the key unset reports all checks passed. Those 95 entries are an honest legacy prefix that predates HMAC signing being enabled — a missing `sig`, not a present-but-invalid one.

`walkChainForStoreHash` (packages/tickets/lib/doctor.mjs:95) applies a blanket rule: with a key configured, EVERY entry must carry a valid signature. It fails on line 1.

This is policy drift between three implementations of one rule:

- `packages/gate-manifest/lib/verify.mjs` implements the contiguous-legacy-prefix rule via `seenSignedEntry`, exposed as `--allow-legacy-unsigned`.
- `chainIsIntact` in `packages/tickets/lib/manifest-segments.mjs` implements the SAME rule, in this very package, added by an adversarial-review finding (T-MANIFEST-FOREST eighth round).
- `walkChainForStoreHash` in doctor.mjs never got it. Its header notes it mirrors gate-manifest's `entrySigValid` byte-for-byte because `tickets <- core <- gate-manifest` would cycle; it mirrored the function but not the policy around it.

Effect: a shipped diagnostic is permanently red on honest history. It fails safe (a false RED, not a false green), but a check that is always red is a check operators learn to ignore.

## The second half — do not merely silence it

`storeHashBindingCheck` sets `check.signaturesVerified = key !== null` and `check.authenticated = key !== null`. Those claims are sound TODAY only because the walk is strict. Making the walk lenient without further change would turn them into false claims whenever the bound checkpoint came from an unsigned entry — converting a false-red into a false-green, which is this suite's signature risk.

So leniency in the chain walk must be paired with strictness in the trust decision: with a key configured, only an entry whose signature VERIFIED may supply `boundStoreHash`. This mirrors the per-entry filter `manifest-segments.mjs` already applies for the identical laundering reason (an unsigned forged entry must not be laundered into trust by a later, unrelated, genuinely signed append).

On this repo that costs nothing: every entry that actually carries `data.storeHash` is signed (root line 185, and every segment's). But the fix must not depend on that accident.

## Fix

In `walkChainForStoreHash`:

1. Track `seenSignedEntry` per chain. A MISSING signature is tolerated only while no earlier entry in THIS chain carried a valid one; after that it is `MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, exactly as today.
2. A PRESENT-but-invalid signature stays `MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID` at ANY position, including inside the prefix.
3. Adopt `data.storeHash` into `boundStoreHash` only when `key === null` (nothing is verifiable, existing keyless behaviour) or the entry's own signature verified.
4. If a key is set and the only checkpoints seen were unsigned, report `bound: false` with a reason naming that, not the generic "no evidence-required transaction recorded yet".

## Acceptance criteria

1. A chain with an unsigned prefix followed by signed entries passes the check with a key set.
   Verify: `node --test packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs` — a new case writes a two-entry ledger (entry 1 unsigned, entry 2 signed and carrying the live storeHash) and asserts `check.ok === true` and `check.boundStoreHash` equals the signed entry's storeHash.
2. An unsigned entry AFTER a signed one still fails.
   Verify: same file — entry 1 signed, entry 2 unsigned; asserts `check.ok === false` and `code === 'MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID'`.
3. A present-but-invalid signature inside the legacy prefix still fails.
   Verify: same file — entry 1 carries a `sig` that does not verify; asserts `code === 'MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID'`.
4. An unsigned legacy entry cannot supply the bound checkpoint when a key is set.
   Verify: same file — a single unsigned entry carrying the live storeHash; asserts `check.bound !== true` and that `check.authenticated` is not asserted true over an unverified checkpoint.
5. The existing contract is unchanged: the in-place final-entry edit case and the validly-signed case still behave as before.
   Verify: all pre-existing cases in `packages/tickets/test/doctor.test.mjs` pass unmodified.
6. `adlc ticket doctor` passes on this repository with `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` exported.
   Verify: run it on the repo root; exit 0, all checks pass.
7. Full suite and preflight green.
   Verify: `env -u ADLC_TICKET node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0 at 54/54; `env -u ADLC_TICKET node scripts/preflight.mjs` exits 0.

## Non-goals

- Not adding an `--allow-legacy-unsigned` flag to doctor. The prefix rule is correct by default and strictly stronger than blanket leniency; a flag operators must remember is a worse default.
- Not re-signing the 95 legacy entries (`gate-manifest migrate --attest-unsigned`). That backdates trust in an audit ledger — asserting entries were signed when signing did not yet exist — and destroys the honest signal that they predate it. The manifest root is frozen in forest mode besides.
- Not de-duplicating the three copies of this rule. Real, but a larger refactor across a dependency cycle; out of scope here.
title: doctor's storeHash binding must tolerate an honest legacy unsigned prefix, and bind only to signed entries
